pull.title: KAFKA-21318, KAFKA-20292: Compute GroupSpecImpl's assigned partitions lazily
pull.body:
Replace GroupSpecImpl's inverted target assignment with a BitSet of the
assigned partitions of each topic, computed from the members' current
assignments on the first call to isPartitionAssigned. Only the uniform
homogeneous assignor calls isPartitionAssigned, so other assignors no
longer compute it.

This makes build in TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark ~40% faster for
homogeneous groups, because isPartitionAssigned no longer looks up
partitions in the inverted target assignment's TimelineHashMaps, which
are slower than regular maps.

It also fixes a bug where the assignor saw the partitions of members
removed in the same request as still assigned. The bug is not reachable
today, since we do not compute a new target assignment when a member
leaves, only on the next heartbeat, and static member replacement keeps
the replaced member's partitions assigned.

Remove ModernGroup's inverted target assignment, since it is no longer
read. For share groups, it was never correct, because a partition can be
assigned to several members of a share group, while the inverted target
assignment holds a single member per partition.

Rename buildAssignment in TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark to
buildGroupSpecAndAssignment, which builds a new group spec on every
invocation, so that the cost of computing the assigned partitions is
included, and replace buildGroupSpecWithoutOffload and
buildGroupSpecWithOffload with an assignorOffload parameter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: David Jacot <dajac@apache.org>

review_comments.body: We should get rid of this when https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23888 is merged. We already trust the caller in a few other places in this class so it does not seem to hurt.

I don't like this because it does not look like a builder anymore. That being said, `uniform2` does not use `isPartitionAssigned` at all. Should we just leave those tests as they were? We could thrown an exception if that method for instance. If we want to keep it, we should switch to using `MetadataImageBuilder` in the tests now. It does not make sense to hide it in this class anymore.
Should we measure with and without offloading?
ditto.
I suppose that it does not matter but if the topic does not exist anymore, the method returns false now. We may want to update the javadoc.
I wonder if storing the partition count next to the bitset is worth it here. I am not sure about it.
It's less churn if we pass an empty metadata image in `GroupSpecFixture`. Did that instead.
We can. Soon there won't / shouldn't be a difference, so it would be solely for catching regressions.
Updated the javadoc.

We can be more precise in dropping non-existent partitions by doing a 2nd pass through the map afterwards. It keeps the number of metadata image lookups limited too.

The homogeneous runs become a tiny bit slower but still an overall improvement.

`uniform` assignor, `partitionsToMemberRatio=50`, `topicCount=100`, 2 warmup and 2 measurement iterations of 5s, ms/op.

| memberCount | subscriptionType | TimelineHashMap `build` | Lazy assignedPartitions `build` | Change |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------ |
| 5000        | HOMOGENEOUS      | 6.180                   | 3.886                           | -37%   |
| 5000        | HETEROGENEOUS    | 10.618                  | 12.212                          | +15%   |
| 10000       | HOMOGENEOUS      | 14.781                  | 8.800                           | -40%   |
| 10000       | HETEROGENEOUS    | 27.686                  | 30.261                          | +9%    |
I will address `topicAssignablePartitionsMap` in #23896. I'm not sure which places you mean where we trust the caller?
I meant that we don't make a defensive copy of all the data structures that we get (e.g. the assignments).

Have you considered storing `metadataImage.topicMetadata(topicId).map(CoordinatorMetadataImage.TopicMetadata::partitionCount).orElse(0)` next to the `BitSet`? We could have a small record (BitSet, int) and then use it in the condition instead of `assignedPartitions.size()`. Would it work?
I considered it but was not a fan of it. Unless we make another pass through the map, we would hold on to the records after the method returns when we no longer need the extra data.

I see. The way I see it, the contents of the record types (`Assignment`, `ResolvedRegularExpression`) and `Member` classes are immutable by convention (yes, I'm aware it's convention only!), so we can assume they are safe to re-use, without having to reason about the caller. Whereas the same principle doesn't hold for a `Map`.

Let's move this discussion to the next PR!
The loop per say does not bother me too much. However, I don't like the second lookup to the image.

> Whereas the same principle doesn't hold for a Map.

This is fair. We could wrap the Map to make it clearer, I guess.
Switched to an approach where we cache partition counts temporarily in a separate map. What are your thoughts on this?

Hmm... Isn't two lookups per topic unecessary? We already allocate a BitSet so I am not sure to understand why allocating a small record with the bitset and an int is that problematic. It will only live during the execution of the assignor, which is short.
Updated to use a record class. It is subjective but I really do not like it and think it's ugly.
Why do you think so?
It's really the extra wrapper.

commit.message:
MINOR: Compute GroupSpecImpl's assigned partitions lazily

Replace GroupSpecImpl's inverted target assignment with a BitSet of the
assigned partitions of each topic, computed from the members' current
assignments on the first call to isPartitionAssigned. Each BitSet is
sized to the topic's partition count in the metadata image, and
partitions beyond it are dropped. Only the uniform homogeneous assignor
calls isPartitionAssigned, so other assignors no longer compute it, and
GroupSpecBuilder no longer copies the inverted target assignment when
assignor offload is enabled.

When a request removes a member and runs the assignor, the assignor
now sees the removed member's partitions as unassigned. Previously, it
saw them as assigned, because the group's inverted target assignment
is only updated when the request's records are replayed.

This makes build in TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark 48-54% faster for
homogeneous groups of 5000 and 10000 members, because
isPartitionAssigned no longer looks up partitions in the inverted
target assignment's TimelineHashMaps, which are slower than regular
maps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MINOR: Remove ModernGroup's inverted target assignment

The inverted target assignment is no longer read since GroupSpecImpl
computes the assigned partitions from the group spec's members. Stop
maintaining it on every target assignment update.

For share groups, it was never correct, because a partition can be
assigned to several members of a share group, while the inverted
target assignment holds a single member per partition.

issue.title: MINOR: Use a SmallIntegerSet to copy the group spec for assignor offload

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Add SmallIntegerSet, an immutable BitSet-backed set of small integers,
and use it to copy the assigned and assignable partitions into the group
spec when the assignor is offloaded. GroupSpecImpl now holds the
assigned partitions of each topic instead of the inverted target
assignment, since assignors never read the owner of a partition.

This makes buildGroupSpecWithOffload 23-55% faster in
TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark with 5000 and 10000 members.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: KAFKA-20292: Avoid copying share group assignable partitions in GroupSpecBuilder

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Pass the share group state partition metadata to ShareGroupSpecBuilder
and look up assignable partitions in a ShareGroupSpecImpl subclass,
instead of copying the initialized partitions into GroupSpecImpl on
every share group assignment, and again for assignor offload. The
metadata is unmodifiable, so no copy is needed.

With that copy gone, the group spec builders no longer copy anything for
assignor offload, so remove the assignorOffload flag from the consumer,
share and streams group spec builders. The tests that covered offload
now check that group specs are not affected by modifications made after
they are built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: David Jacot <dajac@apache.org>
